raw_response:
I am 72 years old. I never went to school, not one day. My father taught me farming, and I have done it for 55 years. I have 15 mu of land in Quzhou County. Twelve mu I plant wheat in October and maize in June after the wheat is cut. Three mu I plant cotton in spring. I have six people in my house. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money home, but the farm must pay for itself. My wife and I do the work. We hire no one.

For the wheat, I buy Jimai 22 from the seed dealer. It is an improved variety. I have used it for many years. Old Wang across the road uses it and gets good yield, so I copy him. I plough the land before sowing. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg a bag. That is 7.5 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphate, and 7.5 kg of potash in each bag. Then at jointing time in March or April, I spread one bag of urea per mu. The urea is 46 percent nitrogen, so one 50 kg bag is about 23 kg of nitrogen. In total I put about 30 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphate, and 8 kg of potash per mu. I irrigate four times: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once in winter to protect the crop from cold, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice — once for aphids and once if I see yellow rust on the leaves. I expect to get about 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For the maize, after I cut the wheat in early June, I plant the maize right away. I buy hybrid seeds from the dealer — the same yellow bag everyone buys. You cannot save maize seeds, everyone knows that. The plants will not grow right. I do not till the land. I plant into the wheat stubble. That is what everyone does now. It saves time and diesel. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant, then at the big trumpet stage I put one bag of urea per mu. That is about 22 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphate, and 5 kg of potash per mu. I irrigate three times: after sowing, at big trumpet, and when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide two times for the corn borers. If they are bad I spray a third time. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

For the cotton, I plant 3 mu. I use my own saved seeds. I have been saving them for many years. They are not fancy but they work. I plough the land in spring. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and about 20 kg of urea per mu when the flowers come out. That is about 15 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphate, and 5 kg of potash per mu. Cotton needs more spraying than grain — I spray four times for bollworms and aphids. The bollworms are bad some years. I irrigate three times. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive now. Last year urea went up by 20 yuan a bag. But I would rather put a little too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family. Wasting some fertilizer is just money down the drain. I watch what Old Wang and the others do. If they put more this year, I will put more too. When I am unsure, I do what I did last year. Change is risky.
